correctness.rationale: The complete cone surface area follows from the four edge-to-apex triangular-face formulas and the base area 6; volume is 2h. The two slanted-face terms are an even strictly convex function of the transverse coordinate, forcing y=0. On that plane, minimizing the scale-invariant ratio is equivalent to minimizing Phi=A/h^(2/3). Coercivity gives existence. For any level c, G_c=A-c h^(2/3) is convex; strictness in h when heights differ and strict convexity of A in x at fixed h rule out two global minimizers. If Phi is stationary at (x,h), then G_c has value zero and zero gradient there for c=Phi(x,h), so convexity makes that point a global minimizer. Therefore the stationary system has exactly one solution and it is the unique global optimum. The packaged checker independently evaluates that solution and reproduces the source's fixed-height numerical data.

value.rationale: The object is the source's own canonical nontriangular counterexample, introduced specifically to demonstrate that the triangle theorem does not extend naively. The source relied on numerical experiments for the globally optimal cone. Proving that the observed point is the unique global optimizer converts the motivating example from numerical evidence to a theorem and supplies a reusable strict-sublevel-convexity mechanism for fixed-base cone-apex optimization.
